title: Arrow comparison for canonical module base change in explicit affine charts
statement: Choose shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] and additive tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let (g′:X′→X,f′:X′→S′,f:X→S,g:S′→S) be cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], G any module, and c an IsDerivedModulePullbackComparison [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. For affine V⊆S and W⊆S′ with W⊆g⁻¹(V), construct U=f⁻¹(V), A=Γ(S,V), B=Γ(S′,W), fA=(f restricted to V) followed by V.isoSpec.hom, gA=W.isoSpec.inv followed by g.resLE and V.isoSpec.hom, and H=schemeOpenRestriction(X,U)(G) [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. There exists a canonical comparison c0 for the chosen pullback of fA and gA, together with source and target isomorphisms a,b in D(W), such that R(β followed by Rf′_*(c)) followed by b.hom equals a.hom followed by T(βA followed by RfA′_*(c0)), where R is derived restriction to W, T is the derived direct image of W.isoSpec.inv, and β,βA are the canonical derived mates [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. No flatness, quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, separatedness, or invertibility assumption occurs.

proof.text: Construct the displayed U, A, B, fA, gA and H from the actual opens and spectrum charts. The cartesian universal property identifies pullback(fA,gA) with the full inverse image of W under f′, after inserting the W chart. This isomorphism preserves the projection to U and the projection to Spec B.

Derived pullback composition and exact open restriction identify the source after transport to D(W). Full-inverse-image restriction of derived direct image and direct-image composition identify the target. Both comparison chains are isomorphisms. Take their components as a and b.

Unpack hc into its witnessing left-derived counit. Restrict and transport that counit through the projection-preserving pullback isomorphism, using exactness of open/chart restriction and the termwise tensor restriction identification. The left-derived universal property gives the affine counit. Its component followed by the single-complex identification defines c0 and proves its comparison predicate. No arbitrary independent counit is selected.

Apply the underived open-square mate identity to the termwise pullbacks. The derived adjunction equations and the coherence of the composition comparisons transport that identity through localization and the charts. They identify the canonical derived base-change arrows, not just their endpoints. Compose with the transported counit c0 to obtain R(β≫Rf′_*(c))≫b.hom=a.hom≫T(βA≫RfA′_*(c0)). The same calculation works for the empty open and arbitrary modules.
